title: Double check of deploy 5d65566: the theme name fits its column; New World accent buttons carry white labels

source.ref: Double check of the 2026-11-04 production deploy 5d65566 (Daniel: 'Double check everything'), rendered at 390, 1280 and 2000. Report: /mnt/project-files/double-check-2026-11-04/REPORT.md

detail: The Nocturne-layout theme pages size the theme name at clamp(44px,17cqw,112px), which assumes a short name. At 390, CyberWitch measured 414px in a 339px column and the page clipped it to 'CyberWitc'; at 1280 CyberWitch (621px), New World (558px) and Wildheart (516px) all ran past their 509px column, the last letters under the surface chips and the browser frame. The heading now sets --nwf-chars to its length and the sheet caps the size at 130cqw per character (min 40px), so a name shrinks only when it would not fit: Bold is unchanged, the three long names fit at 390, 1280 and 2000 (measured 316/475/469px for CyberWitch). Probe: node scripts/probes/theme-name-fits-phone.mjs. Second finding, Daniel's call on the card (2026-11-04, 'White labels everywhere'): New World's Night register put ink on its filled accent buttons (the zip's --text-on-accent), so 'Book your first visit', 'Send', 'Join' and 'Join the list' read dark on Tide teal. NEW_WORLD_ON_ACCENT is white, the Night tokens --nw-accent-text and --nw-text-on-accent are white, a custom owner accent gets ink only when white reads under 2:1 on it, and the shared Services accent button reads the on-accent token on a New World site instead of the white pill's ink. The contrast pin in lib/theme/new-world.test.ts was rewritten on that phrase (white on Tide is 2.6:1, named in the test).
